topics.title: Deductible vs Out-of-Pocket Max in 40 Seconds
topics.hook: Most people think hitting their deductible means 100% free medical care. That misunderstanding costs thousands.

breakdown.stage_1: Deductible: You pay 100% until you reach this threshold.
breakdown.stage_2: Coinsurance: Insurer splits bill (e.g. 80/20) up to the max.
breakdown.stage_3: Out-of-Pocket Max: Insurer finally covers 100% of covered in-network claims.

topics.takeaway: Your deductible is the starting line for coverage; your out-of-pocket maximum is the actual finish line.
topics.disclaimer: General education only, not insurance advice.

topics.title: Where Does Your Health Insurance Premium Go?
topics.hook: Federal law legally forces health insurance companies to spend 80 to 85 cents of every dollar you pay on one thing.

breakdown.aca_80_20_rule: Medical Loss Ratio threshold triggers refund checks if violated.

topics.takeaway: If an insurer spends less than 80% on actual patient care, they must mail you a rebate check.
topics.disclaimer: General education only, not insurance advice.

topics.title: Why Car Insurance Rates Spike (Even With Zero Tickets)
topics.hook: Zero accidents, zero speeding tickets, pristine record—yet your auto renewal jumped 18%. Why?

breakdown.sensor_bumpers: +34% average bumper replacement cost due to radar and cameras
breakdown.weather_loss_events: Hail and flood claims spread across entire zip code rating pools

topics.takeaway: Insurance is a collective pool: you pay for the replacement tech and claim frequency of everyone around you.

topics.title: The Mortgage Amortization Curve: Month 1 vs Year 15

breakdown.year_15_shift: Payment gradually flips to majority principal reduction

topics.takeaway: In the early years, you are essentially renting cash from the bank. One extra annual payment cuts years off the loan.

topics.title: What Actually Determines Your Credit Score?
topics.hook: Closing an old credit card can drop your credit score 30 points overnight. Here is the mathematical reason why.
topics.takeaway: Closing old cards cuts your total credit limit and shortens your average history.
topics.disclaimer: General education, not credit repair advice.

topics.title: APR vs APY: The Hidden Difference Banks Use
topics.hook: Notice how banks quote APR when you borrow, but APY when you save? There's a calculated mathematical reason.

breakdown.apr: Annual Percentage Rate (simple interest, excludes compounding)
breakdown.apy: Annual Percentage Yield (reflects frequency of compounding interest)
breakdown.impact: A 5% APY pays more than a 5% APR over 12 months.

topics.takeaway: When borrowing: lower APR is better. When saving: higher APY with daily compounding is better.

topics.title: What 3% Inflation Does to $10,000 Over 10 Years
topics.hook: Leaving $10,000 cash in a 0.01% checking account feels safe. Mathematically, it is a guaranteed loss.

breakdown.purchasing_power_loss: Drops to ~$7,374 in real goods and services
breakdown.annual_hidden_tax: ~$260 to $300 in lost purchasing power each year

topics.takeaway: Inflation is the invisible friction fee on cash. High-yield savings or diversified assets protect purchasing power.

topics.title: Where Is Your Money Really Safe? (FDIC Explained)
topics.hook: If your bank collapses on Friday afternoon, is your cash gone on Monday morning?

breakdown.coverage_limit: $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category
breakdown.fintech_caution: Neobanks use partner banks; check if funds are held in sweep accounts.

topics.takeaway: Always confirm the FDIC member bank logo; cash in insured banks is backed by the full faith and credit of the US government.
